title: trqp: context.time parsed twice
description:
git-vouch-trqp:194-196 and :267-268. check_payload calls parse_time(time, "payload.context.time") only to validate and discards the datetime. respond() then calls parse_time on the same string with the same label to get `at`. That is two parses, and two places that must agree on the label and the blank-means-now rule.

What goes wrong if left: a future change to the time rule (for example vouch-faq3.13's clamping, or a skew bound on context.time) has to be made in both places. If only one is changed, validation and use drift apart.

Rewrite: have check_payload return the parsed value and the original string:

    def check_payload(payload) -> tuple[Optional[str], Optional[datetime]]:
        ...
        if context.get("time"):  # the registry schema: blank means now
            time = context["time"]
            at = parse_time(time, "payload.context.time")
    ...
    time, at = check_payload(payload)   # respond(), replacing lines 267-268

The original string is still echoed as time_requested.
